title: CCBs for Heart Failure with Preserved EF: A Multicenter RCT
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart Failure with Preserved EF represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. CCBs has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in heart failure with preserved ef. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter rct involving 1,200 participants with confirmed heart failure with preserved ef (mean age 59 years, 42% male). Participants were randomized to receive either ccbs or standard care. The primary endpoint was composite clinical endpoint. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 6 months. RESULTS: Treatment with ccbs resulted in a 44% relative improvement in composite clinical endpoint versus standard care (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.65-0.69, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 40 percentage points (NNT = 16). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 20% of the treatment group versus 13% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 7% and 7% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: CCBs demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for heart failure with preserved ef, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of ccbs into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
